result.title: From Game Generation to Game Playing: Fully Automated Ability Training for Vision-Language-Action Models
result.summary: Training vision-language-action (VLA) models to follow gameplay instructions across diverse games is limited by the cost of collecting demonstrations. We introduce a framework that automatically generates game environments and expert demonstrations. An LLM-powered agent uses game-building tools to construct executable environments and tasks targeting specified skills. Programmatic experts then use privileged simulator state to generate aligned instructions, rendered observations, and keyboard and mouse actions. We train our game policy, Script2Play, by post-training a 4B vision-language model with behavior cloning on 150.3 hours of synthetic Minecraft and Roblox gameplay, without human gameplay demonstrations or reinforcement learning. Evaluation on multiple public game benchmarks demonstrates that Script2Play follows gameplay instructions effectively and generalizes across game engines, highlighting the effectiveness of targeted synthetic supervision.

AI.brief_summary: 用 LLM agent 调用游戏构建工具自动生成可执行环境与任务，再由基于特权模拟器状态的程序化专家产出对齐的指令、渲染观测与键鼠动作，以 150.3 小时合成 Minecraft/Roblox 数据做行为克隆，训练 4B 的 VLA 游戏策略 Script2Play。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是游戏动作策略而非视觉推理状态，但其「特权模拟器状态→自动对齐监督」的合成数据管线，可能为 LVR 中可验证中间监督与推理轨迹构造提供借鉴线索，需核查其标注方式能否迁移。
